title: Cortex SessionPromoteOnCloseRequest (DRAFT v0)
description: Canonical wire shape for POST /sessions/{session_id}/promote-on-close on mnemos. The session-run-lifecycle keystone: a Maestro run opens a Mnemos session at start and `promote-on-close` with the attestor = run id. Mirrors the historical main.py:PromoteOnCloseRequest BaseModel but is the SINGLE source of truth per ADR-0014; main.py imports and re-types it. The keystone is `additionalProperties:false` — without it a producer could inject rogue fields (e.g. undeclared provenance metadata, hidden attestor overrides) that consumers would silently pick up. All fields are optional on the wire (defaults are server-side); the keystone declares them as nullable where the legacy Pydantic posture allows None, so the keystone's first pass is shape-only and the handler's second pass enforces the business rules (attestor required for non-empty promote lists, to_container must resolve to a container, etc.). The `promote_memory_ids` items are ULID-shaped server-side strings (no schema constraint to keep the wire format-agnostic — the schema only checks `type:string` and `minLength:1`). Status: DRAFT; bump $id on breaking changes. Note: this is the WRITE shape for the session-close ritual; the server's response carries additional server-stamped fields (promoted_ids, swept_ids, to_container) that are NEVER accepted on input.

promote_memory_ids.description: List of session memory_ids to promote to the durable parent container. None or [] = promote nothing (sweep all unpromoted memories on close). Server-side sweeps (tombstones) the unpromoted remainder.

to_container.description: Target protected-root container for the promoted memories. None = default to the session's parent scope (per db.close_session). Server normalizes via normalize_container_tag().

attestor.description: WHO is attesting this session close is a reviewed ritual (e.g. 'mvs_<run-id>' for a Maestro run). Required at the handler level (400 if absent AND promote_memory_ids is non-empty) but optional on the wire so the keystone can emit a clean 'attestor required for non-empty promote' message before the handler's own check.

reason.description: Free-form WHY this session is being closed. Recorded in the audit log alongside the attestation_id. Optional but encouraged.
